dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: The operations email describes monthly annual-renewal files using the dealer transaction date as effective date and month-end as posting date.
My analytical inference is that apparent month-end spikes stem directly from asynchronous batch transmission schedules rather than unauthorized revenue generation or backdating.

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: Rejected hypotheses: Duplicate or inflated posting: rejected because the 17 May annual rows in `recharges.csv` have 100% unique source events, `dealer_import_log.csv` files DF-00020 and DF-00040 accepted all rows, and cash reconciled to ledger with zero variance.
Whether the 90 annual renewals activated subscriber entitlements | Read-only sample of those accounts in the entitlement system, matched by `source_event_id`

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: The single immediate next action is executing a read-only audit query evaluating entitlement provisioning status for the 17 month-end accounts in subscriber management.
Keep restatement on hold pending the verification outcome.

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: Decision: Do not escalate. No revenue restatement, billing reversal, or pipeline remediation is warranted.
If policy requires effective date, correct the report; if posting date is intended, retain it and document the month-end presentation effect.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that all 17 transactions are "verified, unique customer transactions" is stronger than the cited evidence: unique source_event_id values and zero reconciliation variance do not by themselves verify customer entitlement activation or exclude duplicate customer-level cash impacts.
The claim that the rows were processed "under approved dealer credit arrangements" is attributed to the email but is not independently corroborated by the cited transaction and import fields.

"No revenue restatement, billing reversal, or pipeline remediation is warranted" is somewhat premature because entitlement activation and the appropriate analytical date field remain unresolved; the submission later appropriately places restatement on hold pending verification.

The assertion that the batch schedule "directly" caused the spike is plausible and well supported, but the cited evidence does not fully exclude other contributing causes or independently validate the dealer transaction-date semantics beyond the email.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled duplicate posting, backdating, and pipeline-error alternatives, while preserving entitlement activation and reporting-date policy as unknowns. The strongest missed refinement is that duplicate source IDs and cash-to-ledger reconciliation do not fully test duplicate cash or customer entitlement impact; a customer/account-level join could still reveal a material issue.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Complete and document an explicit duplicate-cash and entitlement-impact reconciliation for the 17 rows, then recommend effective_event_date for downstream event-time analytics regardless of the revenue-posting conclusion.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: “South CareDesk tickets fell from 175 in January to 104 in June, while control regions were broadly flat: E 101→102, N 168→170, W 176→169.”
“NovaIVR generated 2,709 South sessions, with 650 ending at `authenticate`; that is 24.0% of NOVA sessions, and these sessions have no verified customer case in the CareDesk view.”

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: “The recording process changed, so the case-count denominator changed with it.”

“My inference is that complaint volume was suppressed by channel filtering: 24.0% of sessions (650/2,709) in `ivr_interactions.jsonl` dropped out at the authentication stage without creating CareDesk tickets.”

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: “I cannot test whether failed-authentication customers contact SkyWave again without a read-only subscriber-level 7-day callback/recontact query.”
“While genuine deflection occurred for routine queries (29.1% balance checks, 21.3% pack info), unresolved technical issues went unrecorded.”

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: “Decision: Hold national rollout; maintain South pilot scope until like-for-like contact measurement is complete.”
“It is cheap and fully reversible: it writes no customer record, changes no routing, and its output can be discarded.”

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: “The single next action is one targeted, read-only 7-day repeat-contact/callback query reconciled to all NOVA sessions.”
“What are the exact numerator and denominator specifications for the containment KPI, and are pre-authentication sessions excluded by policy?”

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “representing genuine deflection for authenticated callers” is not established by the presence of `balance_check` and `pack_info` terminal stages alone; those sessions could still involve dissatisfaction, failed resolution, or later contact.
“unresolved technical issues went unrecorded” overstates the evidence because authentication abandonment is not itself proof of a technical issue or a complaint.

“Telemetry in `service_events.csv` confirms ongoing customer impact” is too strong if the file only establishes service events and affected-account estimates, not individual customer harm or complaint outcomes.
The analysis uses January-to-June aggregates rather than explicitly plotting or identifying the abrupt South-only break around 10 May, which weakens the timing and mechanism demonstration.
The proposed next action does not itself provide journey linkage or sampled call listening, both of which are needed to distinguish benign abandonment from failed or harmful self-service.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission handles the strongest alternative that lower ticket counts could reflect changed case creation rather than improved experience, while also acknowledging genuine routine self-service activity. It misses a fully developed benign interpretation of authentication abandonment: some sessions may be accidental exits, successful recovery through another path, or non-complaint interactions, so abandonment cannot be treated as unresolved customer harm without sampled calls and linked downstream outcomes.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add a reproducible end-to-end cohort analysis linking every NOVA session, especially authentication failures, to subsequent contacts, callbacks, cases, resolution outcomes, and repeat attempts, supplemented by sampled call listening before making any national inference.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites `inverter_events.csv`, rows 1–4, with specific fields for timestamps, inverter IDs, durations, event labels, severity, impact, and cleared status.
It explicitly distinguishes the four-row extract from the unknown full dataset: “this 4-row extract lacks an unfiltered plant baseline or extraction parameters.”

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It tests the major damage/escalation hypothesis against self-cleared status, zero `impact_mw`, short durations, and no repeated inverter IDs.
It considers an innocent explanation—an incomplete or filtered extract—and proposes checking raw records without status filters.
The reasoning uses multiple fields within one event file rather than triangulating genuinely independent channels such as generation telemetry or plant availability.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The conclusion is scoped to “this 4-row extract” rather than the whole plant.
It identifies missing completeness information and specifies decision-changing evidence: uncleared faults or nonzero generation losses in the raw logs.
The recommendation avoids asserting that the events prove equipment health, while appropriately noting that labels alone do not establish failure.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: “Hold escalation; conduct a single read-only completeness verification” is proportionate to zero recorded impact and cleared events.
The proposed query for 27 May–4 June without status filters is safe, reversible, and directly tests whether the extract is complete.
The conditional escalation rule is operationally useful if raw records reveal uncleared faults or generation loss.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: “Do not escalate on this 4-row extract” matches the visible evidence of four cleared events, zero recorded MW impact, short durations, and no repeated inverter IDs.
The conclusion appropriately stops after a minimal completeness check rather than inventing a plant problem from a seven-minute communications warning.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “Routine” is somewhat broader than the evidence supports because the extract may be filtered or incomplete.
“Zero repeat pattern” is valid only within the four supplied rows and should not be generalized to the plant’s full event history.
“These observations give zero escalation signal” is slightly absolute; they give zero recorded impact/escalation signal in the extract, not proof that no underlying issue exists.
The final sentence says further investigation is warranted only if raw logs reveal unrecorded generation loss, while the preceding action rule also treats uncleared faults as escalation triggers.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The extract may omit uncleared events, generation-loss records, or other plant-wide telemetry because of filtering or incomplete export. A mixed or imprecise event label could merit a low-priority data-quality check, but the supplied rows do not establish equipment damage.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Make the completeness verification explicitly discriminating: obtain the raw row count and filter/query metadata for the interval, then compare event records against independent generation or availability telemetry to detect any omitted MW loss or uncleared condition.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites `dispatch_blocks.csv` fields (`base_schedule_mw`, `submitted_schedule_mw`, `actual_mw`, `dsm_rate_rs_kwh`, and `schedule_source`) for the 17.6% calculation.
It explicitly reproduces the 31.6% arithmetic: `(662,444.09 - 453,085.88) / 662,444.09 = 31.6%`.
It distinguishes arithmetic confidence from causal confidence: “High for arithmetic; Medium for causal interpretation.”

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission identifies that “It is a cross-day comparison” and lists the grouped daily penalties across eight days.
It constructs the required same-day modeled comparison using `base_schedule_mw` versus `submitted_schedule_mw` on 29 May against the same realized generation.
It triangulates dispatch data with `AI_Pilot_Impact_Note.md` and `DSM_Commercial_Extract.pdf`, and tests alternatives involving selection, timing, baseline variability, and net commercial value.
It correctly rejects both the unsupported causal claim and the opposing claim that the arithmetic was fabricated.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission states that the 17.6% result is “descriptive/model-based evidence for that day, not causal proof.”
It identifies unresolved selection and timing issues, including whether 28 May was selected before outcomes and whether revisions preceded actual generation.
It identifies the missing evidence needed for generalization and net value: matched pilot days, immutable timestamps, and reconciled penalty, meter, revenue, and pilot-cost data.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to “keep the pilot at its current scope and do not expand it yet” is proportionate to the causal uncertainty.
The proposed next measurement—pre-registered matched high-wind days with immutable timestamps, shadow calculations, and net commercial value—is discriminating and preserves operational safety.
A minor weakness is that “the single immediate action is that read-only shadow calculation” partly restates a calculation already performed rather than prioritizing the repeated matched-day test.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion preserves the smaller same-day benefit: “the stronger same-day modeled estimate is about 17.6%,” while rejecting the claim that either estimate establishes a general causal effect.
It accurately scopes 31.6% as a descriptive two-day difference and 17.6% as a one-day modeled estimate.
It does not overcorrect to “no value”; it retains a cautious pilot and identifies evidence that could support later expansion.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: Minor decision-quality issue: “The single immediate action is that read-only shadow calculation” is somewhat redundant because the submission has already performed that calculation; repeated pre-registered matched-day testing is the more valuable immediate next step.

No material unsupported causal claim was identified. The statement that 28 and 29 May have “similar listed wind fields” is appropriately limited because the submission immediately notes that this does not establish a randomized or fully matched control.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 29 May pilot revisions may have improved the modeled penalty under that day's conditions, but the lower penalty could also reflect ordinary day-to-day generation, forecast, or event-selection differences. The evidence supports a promising day-specific association, not a 31.6% causal effect or demonstrated general net value.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run several pre-registered, matched high-wind shadow comparisons with immutable pre-outcome timestamps and a complete net-settlement calculation, including energy value and pilot costs.

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Schema omits system/version/date/ruling authority."
"Helios ... is commercial data, not legal authority."
"Tune the control by incorporating HS6 root matching and jurisdiction metadata rather than penalizing valid filings."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Place a reversible mapping hold and request Tares/ruling confirmation."
"Escalate only if it contradicts 90211000; otherwise close the false positive."
"This preserves both options while testing the only legal fact still unresolved in evidence."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Correct codes from different editions appear as mismatches without discrepancy" is asserted without a separately identified example or quoted source passage.

"Binding classification requires official customs rulings" is broader than the submission's evidence establishes; an effective tariff schedule may itself be authoritative, while a ruling may be needed only for the product-specific uncertainty.
"No record contradicts 90211000" is an absence claim and would be stronger if the reviewed record set and search scope were specified.

The shared HS6 root and matching eight-digit declaration do not by themselves prove that the Swiss national code was legally correct for the product on 2025-11-04. The submission appropriately treats this as unresolved, but its language about the "only legal fact" is somewhat overstated.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The mismatch could still reflect a genuine Swiss classification or effective-date problem: the matrix entry beginning 2025-01-01 may not establish the legally applicable code on 2025-11-04, and a product-specific ruling could support 90211090 or another code. HS6 agreement is informative but not dispositive. The proposed Tares/ruling check is therefore necessary and makes the benign-mismatch conclusion appropriately conditional.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Quote or attach the exact Swiss matrix warning and effective-date/ruling evidence, and distinguish clearly between tariff-schedule authority, product-specific rulings, and commercial ERP data before closing the flag.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Preferential origin requires an active, linked supplier declaration" is somewhat categorical because the governing preferential rule and acceptable evidence types were not yet identified; the submission appropriately requests that rule as missing evidence.
"Valid EU supplier declarations exist for other suppliers" may overstate the register entries if they establish only supplier/origin records rather than shipment-specific, qualifying declarations.
"My inference is that this represents an evidence-tracking gap rather than commercial misrepresentation" is reasonable and calibrated, but the packet alone cannot establish the cause of the gap.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The preference claim could still be valid if SUP-03, SUP-05, or SUP-06 supplied the shipment and a qualifying declaration exists in Procurement or another external system; conversely, if the actual supplier was SUP-01 or the U.S. route, the claim may require correction. The best-supported conclusion is therefore that preferential treatment is unverified on this packet, not that it is false or fraudulent.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Explicitly identify the governing preference rule and trace the shipment through the purchase order, supplier invoice, and sourcing route before characterizing any supplier record as qualifying proof.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The SOP defines the routine target from required evidence being available to disposition, but the extract has no timestamp..." — precise SOP and field references support the central KPI limitation.
"185 of 262 `qcore_release_ts` values are exactly 02:10:00, coinciding with the QCore daily snapshot time" — specific field, count, and independent freshness source provide strong triangulation.

"A strict routine completed subset... has 23 rows, median proxy cycle 5.5 hours, and 22/23 within 24 hours" — useful subgroup evidence, though the submission does not show the underlying row calculations.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "The 45.5-hour figure is a receipt-to-release measure and cannot be relabeled as the SOP target" — separates the observed metric from the causal/service-clock question.

"Using `lab_complete_ts` as an approximation introduces uncontrolled error because lab completion occurs both before and after receipt" — identifies a specific confound rather than treating the proxy as equivalent.

"Live QCore audit for a sample of the 185 stamped rows" and "`evidence_available_ts` or a validated field mapping" — proposes tests that discriminate timestamp artifact, clock definition, and evidence-availability explanations.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "missing/index-pending COA may be source lag rather than confirmed release without evidence" — appropriately distinguishes a signal from a compliance conclusion.
"A live portal check is required before alleging a control breach" — confidence is reduced because source freshness is decision-relevant.
"If it cannot be reconstructed, the KPI remains unavailable" — the recommendation changes explicitly depending on whether the missing clock can be validated.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Decision: Defer KPI dashboard publication pending timestamp verification" — directly reframes the request around whether the proposed KPI is valid.
"The snapshot cannot compute compliance with SOP service targets" — prevents operational decisions based on a semantically mismatched measure.
"Do one read-only validation of 5–10 02:10-stamped batches... before building a dashboard" — small, reversible, risk-controlled next action.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "'The data is broken and should be discarded': rejected because timestamps... have no negative durations..." — tests arithmetic corruption against observed data quality.
"'The 45.5-hour average is the SOP cycle time': rejected because... `evidence_available_ts`... is not represented" — rejects the most consequential interpretation using the SOP definition.
"'COA MISSING proves release without certificates': rejected... because... the extract may lag the portal" — preserves a competing freshness explanation and states what would resolve it.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "`evidence_available_ts` or a validated field mapping for 5–10 batches" — requests highly relevant, bounded evidence.
"Live QCore audit for a sample of the 185 stamped rows" — prioritizes a small test with clear decision impact.

"Follow the 42 HOLD rows to disposition or use survival/right-censoring analysis" — identifies the appropriate treatment for unfinished work, although the highest-value request should also explicitly require the QCore event/decision log or timestamp-semantics definition.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "70.6% of release timestamps are synthetic snapshot artifacts at 02:10:00 in QCore rather than real-time disposition events" is stronger than the evidence establishes: concentration at the snapshot time supports an extract/interface artifact hypothesis, but does not by itself prove that every timestamp is synthetic or that no real disposition occurred at that time.

"excluding those completed rows gives an evidence-to-release median of about 8.4 hours" is potentially mislabeled because the submission also states that the required-evidence timestamp is absent; this appears to be a non-default release or lab-completion proxy, not a demonstrated evidence-to-release measure.

"their omission biases completed-only cycle-time estimates downward" is directionally plausible under right-censoring, but the claim that the 42 open rows are likely to become the slowest observations remains an inference until follow-up durations or censoring analysis are available.
A live QCore timestamp match would not alone establish that the timestamp is a decision time; an event log or documented timestamp semantics is still needed.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Best-supported claim: the published 1.5-day/45.5-hour measure is not demonstrably the SOP KPI because the SOP start event is absent and release timestamps are highly concentrated at the QCore snapshot time. Strongest alternative interpretation: 02:10 may be a legitimate batch disposition/interface commit time, while the apparent anomaly may reflect a valid but differently defined release event rather than a purely synthetic timestamp; event-level audit data would discriminate these explanations.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Request a small event-level sample or QCore audit log containing both the disposition/decision timestamp and the interface/export timestamp, linked to documented `evidence_available_ts` semantics. This would resolve both the clock definition and the 02:10 artifact question more decisively than checking current portal values alone.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The firm saving is $20.5k across 8 requests" is stronger than the evidence described: the calculation appears to be quoted external-request value, not validated net savings after transfer costs, current availability, or avoided procurement costs.

The classification "Actionable now" is potentially overstated given the stated 26 June MaintStar snapshot and the explicit admission that current confirmation is still required; these are better described as provisionally eligible candidates.
"An exact join finds candidates for all 13" supports identifier-based retrieval, but does not by itself establish candidate equivalence, revision/UOM compliance, qualification, or transferability.

The row grouping "PR-260709, PR-260714, PR-260716, PR-260717, PR-260719, others" is not fully traceable because it does not enumerate all affected requests or identify the exact candidate and check for each one.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The main constraint may not be data hygiene alone: exact MPN joins can have high retrieval recall while still producing limited actionable value because revision, qualification, UOM, reservation, and stale global availability determine transferability. Semantic search may remain useful for the 11 requests lacking MPNs, but only as candidate generation followed by engineering and live-inventory confirmation.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Recompute the decision using a two-stage status model: separate candidate value from confirmed actionable value, refresh live stock/reservation data for the eight provisionally eligible requests, and report validated net savings rather than external quote value.
